title: Cap. 6 Arg. 7: First Adam's liberty-resolved grace vs Christ's stronger grace that makes willing conquer
pass_a_gloss: For this reason of obtaining or not obtaining salvation, which is resolved into the liberty of human free choice, belonged to the first grace, which was given to the first Adam: as Augustine well observed: but that grace is far more powerful which is given in Christ to all who are to be saved, by which it comes about that they will, and will so much, that in very deed they always conquer the reluctant will of the flesh. (See Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace, chapters 11 and 12.)
pass_b_english: For that account of gaining or missing salvation which resolves into the liberty of human choice belonged to the first grace given to the first Adam—as Augustine well noted. But the grace given in Christ to all who are to be saved is far stronger: by it they will, and will so strongly, that in fact they always overcome the flesh's unwilling will. (See Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace 11-12.)
source_text: Haec enim obtinendae aut non obtinendae salutis ratio, quae in libertatem arbitrii humani resolvitur, fuit primae gratiae, quae data est primo Adamo: ut bene observavit Augustinus: sed haec longe potentior est quae datur in Christo omnibus salvandis, qua fit ut velint, & tantum velint, ut reapse semper vincant reluctantem carnis voluntatem.
